title: How much is it?
summary: Ask for prices with بِكَمْ؟, count from 11 to 100 and say amounts of money in Egyptian pounds.
intro: To ask a price, say بِكَمْ؟ ('for how much?'): بِكَمِ الْمَوْز؟ The tens end in ـُونَ: عِشْرُونَ (20), ثَلَاثُونَ (30), خَمْسُونَ (50); after بِـ they end in ـِينَ: بِعِشْرِينَ. Numbers like 75 are said 'five and seventy': خَمْسَة وَسَبْعُونَ. After 11–99 the noun is singular with -an: عِشْرُونَ جُنَيْهًا (twenty pounds). After مِئَة (100) it is singular too: مِئَةُ جُنَيْه.
objectives: Ask how much something costs with بِكَمْ؟
Count in tens from 20 to 100 and say 11 to 19
Say a price in pounds with the correct form of the noun
Understand a total and your change at a market stall

realLife.title: At the fruit stall
realLife.story: Daniel and Sami buy fruit for the weekend at a stall near the school. The bananas and oranges are cheap, but the mangoes are expensive, and the seller won't lower his price. Daniel pays with a hundred-pound note and checks his change.

sentences.en: How much are the bananas, please?
sentences.literal: for how much (are) the bananas, from your kindness

mistakes.why: After the numbers 11 to 99 the noun is singular with the ending -an: junayhan, not the plural.

sentences.literal: the total (is) five and seventy pound

mistakes.why: From 21 to 99 the unit comes first: 'five and seventy'.

sentences.en: Mangoes are expensive, and oranges are cheap.
sentences.literal: the mango (is) expensive, and the oranges (are) cheap

dialogue.title: Mangoes are too expensive
dialogue.culture: Egypt's money is the pound, جُنَيْه, divided into 100 piastres. At a market stall people often call an older man يَا عَمّ (uncle) as a friendly, respectful address. Gentle bargaining is normal at markets, but not in supermarkets.

lines.ar: أَهْلًا يَا أُسْتَاذ! عِنْدِي فَاكِهَة طَازَجَة الْيَوْم: مَوْز وَبُرْتُقَال وَمَانْجُو.
lines.en: Welcome, sir! I have fresh fruit today: bananas, oranges and mangoes.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر! بِكَمِ الْمَوْز، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
lines.en: Good morning! How much are the bananas, please?

lines.ar: الْمَوْز بِثَلَاثِينَ جُنَيْهًا لِلْكِيلُو، وَهُوَ حُلْوْ جِدًّا.
lines.en: The bananas are thirty pounds a kilo, and they are very sweet.
And the oranges? What is the price of a kilo of oranges?

lines.ar: الْبُرْتُقَال رَخِيص الْيَوْم: عِشْرُونَ جُنَيْهًا فَقَطْ لِلْكِيلُو.
lines.en: Oranges are cheap today: only twenty pounds a kilo.
And the mangoes, sir? How much is a kilo?

lines.ar: الْمَانْجُو بِسِتِّينَ جُنَيْهًا. هٰذَا أَحْسَنُ مَانْجُو فِي مِصْر!
lines.en: Mangoes are sixty pounds. This is the best mango in Egypt!

lines.ar: سِتُّونَ جُنَيْهًا؟ هٰذَا غَالٍ جِدًّا يَا عَمّ! خَمْسُونَ؟
lines.en: Sixty pounds? That is very expensive, sir! How about fifty?

lines.ar: لَا، لَا… الْمَانْجُو غَالٍ هٰذِهِ السَّنَة. سِتُّونَ، آخِرُ كَلَام!
lines.en: No, no… mangoes are expensive this year. Sixty, and that's my final word!

lines.ar: إِذَنْ لَا نُرِيدُ الْمَانْجُو الْيَوْم. أُرِيدُ كِيلُو مَوْز وَكِيلُوَيْنِ مِنَ الْبُرْتُقَال.
lines.en: Then we don't want mangoes today. I'd like a kilo of bananas and two kilos of oranges.

lines.ar: حَاضِر! كِيلُو مَوْز بِثَلَاثِينَ، وَكِيلُوَانِ بِأَرْبَعِينَ. الْمَجْمُوع سَبْعُونَ جُنَيْهًا.
lines.en: Certainly! A kilo of bananas for thirty, and two kilos for forty. That's seventy pounds altogether.
Here you are, this is a hundred pounds.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا! وَهٰذَا الْبَاقِي: ثَلَاثُونَ جُنَيْهًا. مَعَ السَّلَامَة!
lines.en: Thank you! And here is your change: thirty pounds. Goodbye!

lines.ar: مُمْتَاز يَا دَانْيَال! الْآن تَعْرِفُ الْأَسْعَار وَالْأَرْقَام بِالْعَرَبِيَّة.
lines.en: Excellent, Daniel! Now you know prices and numbers in Arabic.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا! وَغَدًا نَشْتَرِي الْمَانْجُو… مِنْ مَحَلّ آخَر!
lines.en: Thanks! And tomorrow we'll buy the mangoes… from another shop!

reading.title: At the fruit stall
reading.ar: الْمَوْز بِثَلَاثِينَ جُنَيْهًا، وَالْبُرْتُقَال بِعِشْرِينَ. الْمَانْجُو غَالٍ: سِتُّونَ جُنَيْهًا لِلْكِيلُو. دَانْيَال يَدْفَعُ سَبْعِينَ جُنَيْهًا، وَالْبَاقِي ثَلَاثُونَ.
reading.en: Bananas cost thirty pounds, and oranges twenty. Mangoes are expensive: sixty pounds a kilo. Daniel pays seventy pounds, and the change is thirty.

quiz.prompt: How much does Daniel's fruit cost altogether?

options: The seller won't lower the price

completion: You did it! You can ask for prices and count to 100. Take the week test to open Week 4.
